File utilities for reading and writing numbers, creating and removing directories, and mapping files.

# Purpose
This C source file implements a small set of file system utility functions for reading, writing, and managing files and directories. It provides helpers to read an unsigned long or unsigned int from a text file, write an unsigned long to a file, read the full contents of a file with `mmap`, and get the path of the current executable from `/proc/self/exe`. These functions use standard POSIX calls such as `open`, `read`, `write`, `close`, `fstat`, `mmap`, and `readlink`, and they return `0` on success or `-1` on error.

The file also includes directory management helpers. [`fd_file_util_mkdir_all`](<#fd_file_util_mkdir_all>) creates a directory path one component at a time, and it can set ownership and permissions on directories that it creates. [`fd_file_util_rmtree`](<#fd_file_util_rmtree>) removes a directory tree by walking entries with `opendir` and `readdir`, deleting files with `unlink`, and removing subdirectories with recursive calls. The code is intended as a reusable utility implementation file, not as an executable, and it exposes file system support functions through `fd_file_util.h`.
